findings.source_quote: ἐκείνοις μὲν ἀντὶ τοῦ πολλοῦ μόχθου παρέσχον τὸ μὴ πλανηθῆναι, ἐξὸν μὴ μοχθῆσαι
findings.english_quote: they have given those people, in exchange for their great toil, only the benefit of not being led astray, though the toil could have been avoided
findings.issue: “Only the benefit” makes not being led astray the exclusive benefit received. The Greek identifies this return for their toil but does not expressly exclude other benefits. μέν participates in the contrast between those who understood and those who were misled; it does not supply this restriction. The criticism of unnecessary toil remains clear without adding “only.”
findings.suggested_revision: Delete “only”: “they have given those people, in exchange for their great toil, the benefit of not being led astray, though the toil could have been avoided.” Submit the revised wording for fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ἅπερ ὑπὸ μόνης ὑπερβαλλούσης φρονήσεως γενέσθαι δυνατὸν ἐστιν καὶ καταληφθῆναι ὑπὸ ἐπιστήμης τῆς μόνης ταῦτα ἀκριβοῦν δυναμένης.
findings.english_quote: These can be brought about only by surpassing intelligence and can be comprehended only by knowledge capable of determining them precisely.
findings.issue: The second μόνης belongs to the attributive phrase describing knowledge as alone capable of determining these things precisely. The draft transfers that exclusivity to “can be comprehended,” introducing a restriction there while failing to preserve its stated attachment to the capability of knowledge. The two occurrences of μόνης should retain their distinct grammatical scopes.
findings.suggested_revision: For fresh review: “These can be brought about only by surpassing intelligence and can be comprehended by knowledge, which alone is capable of determining these things precisely.” This correction requires no change to the supplied Greek.
